$comment: Phase 17 acceptance definition derived from architecture/phase-17-automation-engine.md, the phase contract, automation-core/workflow/actions/governance modules and their four unit suites. Workflow safety is evaluated from executable libraries; no autonomous production execution is inferred.

ownership.note: Phase 17 owns workflow definitions, trigger bindings, run history, action governance and escalation. Transport, domain rules and autonomous self-improvement remain owned elsewhere.

areas.area: Unknown conditions and policy conflicts fail closed
areas.requirement: Automation never treats UNKNOWN or ERROR as permission to proceed, and the highest-priority policy decision controls conflicting rules.

evidence.contains: never treats UNKNOWN as TRUE for any automation
lets the highest-priority policy win on conflict

areas.area: Automation requires explicit authorization and approval
areas.requirement: Operations are authorized for the actor and tenant; high-risk or privileged actions wait for approval and rejected or expired approvals cannot proceed.

evidence.contains: denies AI actors without an explicit role
blocks a required approval until approved
prohibits cross-tenant execution without explicit authorization

areas.area: Workflow definitions and runs are ordered state machines
areas.requirement: Workflow graphs are non-empty DAGs with known dependencies, execution states follow legal transitions and ready steps are resolved topologically.

evidence.contains: blocks an illegal CREATED -> COMPLETED jump

areas.requirement: Non-idempotent steps do not replay, irreversible actions are not blindly retried, compensation is explicit, resource locks recover and deadlocks are detected.

evidence.contains: never re-executes non-idempotent completed steps on replay

areas.area: Actions verify outcomes and can be stopped
areas.requirement: Validation, authorization, preconditions and postconditions precede execution; failed verification is not success, and kill switches and dry-run modes prevent unsafe side effects.

evidence.contains: never reaches execution on authorization failure
never reports failed verification as success
dry-run/simulation/shadow never produce production side effects

areas.area: Workflow activation and production execution remain unwired
areas.requirement: An authorised runtime boundary must invoke activation and action execution; current evidence is limited to the tested automation libraries.
